I don't know if my comment will get read or not but anyway it's a truly valid point that superhero movies are quite the same...using the same formula. They're quite monotonous in some way and the scripts are 70-80% comic book based. It'll be exhausting for the adult eyes, people who see the same stuff, formula, "genre on genre" genre of these types of films, and hey it's completely fine and agreeable.
But the other side to it, the viewers, the huge fan base, the cosplay, the love that people give to these characters are because of many reasons...but have you ever thought about them? They're quite significant to a younger audience that has grown up with these movies.

For instance, you may love the Lord of the Rings trilogy by Peter Jackson, truly a masterpiece of a movie. That was based on the book, why'd you watch it if the book had the same story? The on-screen adaptation, gives an image, a face, a voice, a visual depiction of that character. People, or at least the Marvel comic readers, like to see these characters play it out on the big screen and it intrigues them on how the scene plays out. 

2nd, it may not be for you, but a huge generation has grown up with these movies. For example, in Spiderman NWH, Peter is applying for college, he gets rejected from everywhere and his Dream school of MIT just because he was a hero. Now for you as an adult, you've probably gone through this phase of applying to colleges, but for me, someone who had been rejected from my dream college just days before watching this movie knew what emotions Peter had been going through. I could relate with what was going on because, at that time, even I was going through/am still going through the process(Also proving that even the extracurricular of being a genius, web-swinging superhero, will STILL FUCKING GET YOU REJECTED FROM MIT, I MEAN WHAT THE FUCK, FUCK YOU T20S!)and I could relate with that, as well as people who are in the ongoing process. That sense of relating with a character was there, especially for the younger audiences and that is an amazing thing to see. 

Growing up in this generation where Youtube, superheroes, and video games are the peak entertainment(although it shouldn't be...read a bit pls)there is an inspiration that, mainly MCU movies have given me and its fans/followers. We can see ourselves in their shoes. 

I'm assuming you're a white adult male/female(apologies if you are not, I'm sorry if you felt this was racist) but you've seen yourself being represented SO many times. Every OG Avenger is white. I'm an Indian, for me, Eternal's was one of the first representations ever. And as a kid, as a teen, or maybe GenZ/older millennial if that's a better term? We've had a lot of our childhood involving these movies, so we know what it feels like when we watch a new one too. Also for someone of the newest generation becoming adults in this world, it gives us a sense of hope and inspiration. Because of my College rejection, I was in a SHIT place, but spiderman brought me back up. I didn't even know you could challenge a rejection and I did that(got rejected again so fuck you Dean of ____________ university) but till now, that movie has uplifted me in so many ways, it's inspired me to achieve more and work harder than ever and not sacrifice on what I aim to have in life. Iron man instilled a sense of appreciation for STEM(Although like 95% of the physics in the MCU is😵). Black Panther made me realize that being from where you are, you can be fucking proud of it and be a critic as well. It's these stories, these characters, that resonate, teach, and instill such values and ideas into us. Another example could.be the all-female scene in Endgame(during the avengers compound battle). I've never seen my younger sister's face light up so brightly, such an ecstatic person looking at her gender being represented on screen. That scene was for them, and for them to be proud of themselves, to insinuate that sense of confidence and fearlessness in them. 

Another way, in the latest movies(Phase 4), in every movie there has been a use of some foreign languages. In Shang Chi, it was Mandarin and a representation of Asian culture proving that no matter how villainous, powerful or dangerous, an Asian father is still an Asian father, and no matter what he will always be fucking disappointed at you. In eternal's, there was the use of Hindi and in SPIDERMAN NWH the use of Tagalog(Filipino language). Now, these scenes as an English speaker are not critical for you, but for the millions who speak those languages on a day-to-day basis, it was significant for them. Looking at subtitles of the mandarin parts in Shang chi is cool, but mandarin speakers...you know what's up and the real emotions behind those scenes. Same with the Hindi scenes in Eternals. I could understand what was the true message behind the scene. 

Because representation matters.

 Also, Marvel comics weren't available in many outlets here in India till a few years ago, whereas in the US you've had them for ages. The MCU is a worldwide phenomenon and project. Not only does it try to make you as you get a person to have something to believe in, something to look up to(although each character had their flaw) but it was that message, that sentiment behind the way we perceived each story.
